description: We’re a multidisciplinary team from Koya University combining software engineering, architecture, and petroleum engineering. We’re excited to build a fun, interactive Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer that teaches kids space science through missions and mini-games. Our mix of coding, design, and engineering science lets us create something both educational and engaging. We’re looking for teammates with skills in game development, UI/UX, storytelling, or space science.
summary:
Echoes of Space is an interactive, museum-grade 3D web application developed by software engineering students from Koya University to chronicle humanity’s dormant and historic exploration hardware across the Moon, Mars, and Deep Space.

Addressing NASA’s challenge to give voice to abandoned equipment, we built high-fidelity WebGL 3D models and guided storytelling tours for 13 authentic NASA spacecraft—including Surveyor 3, Apollo 11's Eagle, Ingenuity, Opportunity, and Pioneer 10. The platform features dynamic dual-audience adaptation (Junior Explorer mode for ages 6–12 with synchronized voice narration, and Mission Specialist mode with telemetry and engineering trade-offs) and interactive debrief quizzes.

All coordinates, masses, and mission facts are verified against NASA’s NSSDCA master catalog. These spacecraft are not forgotten scrap; they mark the milestones of human curiosity. Echoes of Space preserves this off-world scientific heritage, inspiring the next generation of engineers and space explorers.
details:
What it does & How it works

Echoes of Space is a WebGL-powered 3D interactive web platform dedicated to humanity's off-world technological heritage. It chronicles 13 historic NASA missions whose hardware remains in situ across the Moon, Mars, and Deep Space.

The application is split into two interconnected layers:

  1. Interactive Planetary Observatory: Users navigate real-time 3D celestial bodies (Moon, Mars, Deep Space) built with procedural surface textures, orbital markers, raycasting, and camera rigs.
  2. Dedicated 3D Exploration Tours: Users launch step-by-step interactive 3D model tours (Surveyor 3, Apollo 11 Lunar Module, Ingenuity, Mars Pathfinder, Opportunity, Pioneer 10, and Kepler). Each model features camera-guided orbital mechanics, interactive component inspection, and real-time audio narration.

Creativity & Unique Value

  • Dual-Audience Inclusivity: A single click toggles between Junior Explorer Mode (ages 6–12, wonder-filled first-person storytelling "I am..." with adjusted vocal pitch) and Mission Specialist Mode (ages 13+, exact NASA telemetry, thrust vectors, radar frequencies, and sensor payloads).
  • Sound-Driven Auto-Scroll: Speech synthesis narration is 100% synchronized with on-screen text. As each audio chapter finishes, the scene automatically smooth-scrolls to the next step, animating the 3D camera across the spacecraft.
  • Mission Debrief Quizzes: Interactive telemetry quizzes at the end of each tour reinforce STEM learning with instant scoring and detailed scientific explanations.

Intended Impact

Abandoned space hardware is often perceived as cosmic junk. Our project reframes these artifacts as humanity's most daring scientific monuments, inspiring youth and students in software engineering and aerospace.

Tools, Languages & Technologies Used

  • Languages: JavaScript (ES6+), HTML5, CSS3.
  • 3D Graphics & Engine: Three.js (WebGL rendering, procedural CanvasTexture generation, glTF asset pipelines).
  • APIs & Accessibility: Web Speech API (SpeechSynthesis), IntersectionObserver, Fullscreen API, responsive mobile/desktop layouts.
  • Hosting & Version Control: Git, GitHub, Local HTTP server testing.
